**sdd/issue-229-c4/design**

**What**: C4 (#229) design — the dualWrite retirement ruling + records-only architecture.
**Why**: Close the transitional window; retire the project's first config key.
**Where**: openspec/changes/issue-229-c4/design.md

Decision 1 (HUMAN-DECIDED, supersedes explore's tolerate-and-ignore lean): retire-by-deletion pre-release, THREE moves — (1) delete gate engram.mjs:176 → record-write unconditional; (2) delete memory.dualWrite from root brain.config.json (propagates via git pull); (3) REMOVE 0.6.0 migration entry (config-migrations.mjs:86-99), CONDITIONED on never-shipped verification CLEAN: commit 654e86c (C2b-1 #223), git tag --contains = NONE, only on feature/v2.0.0, not ancestor of v0.6.0 → deletion honest. Fallback if shipped: inert key + RETIRED marker. DOCTRINE: never-shipped keys retire-by-deletion (free pre-release); post-release retirement (future, not built now) = tolerate-and-ignore+warning; destructive-migration+schemaVersion-bump REJECTED (breaks additive-only, doesn't self-apply). C4 is THIRD slice touching brain/core/config-migrations.mjs (after #215, #223) — no new ceremony.
Decision 2: D2 greenfield records-only pull, per-record engram save + progress, IDEMPOTENT (content-addressed dedup). Decision 3: D4 memory-gate records-only + finding 7 (id:388) deletion→ENOENT fix. Decision 4: D5 precise embargo-end wording.
D1/D4 coupling: gate unions both readers until D4 lands → sequence D4 first, then D3, D2, D1.
OPEN QUESTION: repo's brain.config.json stale at schemaVersion 0.3.0 (3 behind); dualWrite:true set manually not via migrate. Whether to bump/reconcile NOT decidable from ruling — flagged for human, C4 leaves it by default.
**Learned**: Inconsistency surfaced — explore (#391) recommended (b) tolerate-and-ignore; human ruling chose stronger retire-by-deletion, made safe by never-shipped verification. Not a fact conflict.
